name: Static PVs and PVCs
objective: CKA › Storage. Drill EVERY storage corner harder than the exam: StorageClasses (provisioner, reclaimPolicy, binding mode), static PVs with a retain reclaim policy, explicit static PVC binding, mounting a PVC, subPath mounts, the default-class annotation, dynamic provisioning via the default class, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Static PersistentVolume with Retain
questions.teach:
A **PersistentVolume (PV)** is cluster-scoped storage an admin pre-provisions (**static**). Set `capacity.storage`, `accessModes`, `storageClassName`, a backing source (here `hostPath`), and `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain` so the PV (and its data) survives after its claim is deleted.

**Gotcha:** a PV's `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy` is set on the **PV itself** — the StorageClass `reclaimPolicy` only applies to volumes the class *dynamically* provisions, not to this hand-made PV.
questions.prompt:
Create a PersistentVolume `pv-data`: capacity `1Gi`, accessModes `ReadWriteOnce`, `storageClassName: fast-local`, `hostPath` path `/mnt/data`, and `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain`.

Target: `kubectl get pv pv-data` shows a 1Gi RWO Retain volume in class fast-local.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-data
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-local
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data
YAML

verification.description: PV pv-data: 1Gi, RWO, class fast-local, hostPath /mnt/data, reclaimPolicy Retain

questions.title: Static PVC bound explicitly by volumeName
questions.teach:
A **PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)** is a namespaced request for storage. To bind a *specific* PV statically, set `spec.volumeName` to that PV's name; `accessModes`, `storageClassName`, and the requested size must still be satisfiable by the PV. When bound, the PVC shows status `Bound`.

**Gotcha:** if `volumeName` points at a PV whose class or access mode mismatches — or the request exceeds its capacity — the PVC stays `Pending`.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `storage-learn`, create PVC `pvc-data`: request `1Gi`, accessModes `ReadWriteOnce`, `storageClassName: fast-local`, bound explicitly to PV `pv-data` via `volumeName`.

Target: `kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc pvc-data` shows status `Bound` to `pv-data`.
questions.hint: PVC with `spec.volumeName: pv-data`, matching `storageClassName: fast-local`, `accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]`, and `resources.requests.storage: 1Gi`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-data
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-local
  volumeName: pv-data
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
YAML
kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc pvc-data

verification.description: PVC pvc-data is Bound to pv-data

questions.title: Mount the PVC in a pod
questions.teach:
A pod consumes a PVC via `spec.volumes[].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName`, then a container mounts it with `volumeMounts[].mountPath`. Give busybox `sleep 3600` so the pod stays `Running`.

**Gotcha:** if the PVC is `Pending` or missing, the pod never leaves `Pending` — mounting an unbound claim blocks scheduling.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `storage-learn`, create pod `app` (`busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that mounts PVC `pvc-data` at `/data`.

Target: pod `app` reaches `Running` with `pvc-data` mounted at `/data`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: pvc-data
YAML
kubectl -n storage-learn wait --for=condition=Ready pod/app --timeout=60s

verification.description: pod app is Running with pvc-data mounted at /data

questions.title: subPath: mount one sub-directory of a volume
questions.teach:
`volumeMounts[].subPath` mounts a single file or sub-directory of a volume instead of its root — handy to share one PVC across containers without them clobbering each other's paths. The subPath is created inside the volume if it doesn't exist.

**Gotcha:** `subPath` is a field on the **volumeMount**, not the volume; a plain `mountPath` with no `subPath` would expose the whole volume.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `storage-learn`, create pod `sub-app` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that uses PVC `pvc-data` but mounts only its sub-directory `logs` at `/var/log/app` using `subPath: logs`.

Target: pod `sub-app` mounts `pvc-data` at `/var/log/app` with `subPath` = `logs`.
questions.hint: Same `persistentVolumeClaim` volume as before, but the `volumeMounts` entry adds `subPath: logs` alongside `mountPath: /var/log/app`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sub-app
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /var/log/app
      subPath: logs
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: pvc-data
YAML

verification.description: sub-app mounts pvc-data at /var/log/app with subPath logs
